title: 考研英语（旧）2008年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: While still catching up to men in some spheres of modern life, women appear to be way ahead in at least one undesirable category.
sentences.translation: 尽管女性在现代生活的某些领域仍在追赶男性，但她们似乎在至少一个不受欢迎的类别中遥遥领先。纽约退伍军人管理医院首席精神病学家Yehuda博士表示："与男性相比，女性在应对压力时特别容易患上抑郁症和焦虑症。"

sentences.text: "Women are particularly susceptible to developing depression and anxiety disorders in response to stress compared to men," according to Dr. Yehuda, chief psychiatrist at New York's Veteran's Administration Hospital.
Adding to a woman's increased dose of stress chemicals, are her increased "opportunities" for stress.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2008/section2-part-a-1/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好observes, "it's just that they're dealing with so many more things that they become worn out from itmore visibly and sooner."除了女性压力化学物质剂量增加之外，她们承受压力的"机会"也在增加。Yehuda博士说："这并不一定意味着女性应对得不如男性好。只是她们需要应对的事情多得多。"她指出："她们承受压力的能力甚至可能比男性更强，只是她们要处理的事情太多了，因此她们更明显、更快地被压垮。"

sentences.text: "It's not necessarily that women don't cope as well.
It's just that they have so much more to cope with," says Dr. Yehuda.
"Their capacity for tolerating stress may even be greater than men's," she
Not everyone experiences the kinds of severe chronic stresses Alvarez describes.
sentences.translation: 并非每个人都经历Alvarez所描述的那种严重的慢性压力。但如今大多数女性都在应对许多义务，几乎没有休息，并感受到压力。Alvarez的经历表明，在压力威胁到你的健康和行事能力之前找到化解压力的方法是多么重要。

sentences.text: But most women today are coping with a lot of obligations, with few breaks, and feeling the strain.
Alvarez's experience demonstrates the importance of finding ways to diffuse stress before it threatens your health and your ability to function.
It used to be so straightforward.
sentences.translation: 过去这一切都是那么直截了当。一组研究人员在实验室共同工作，将他们的研究成果提交给期刊。期刊编辑随后会将作者的姓名和所属机构从论文中删除,并将其发送给同行进行评审。根据收到的评论意见,编辑会接受该论文发表或拒绝发表。版权归期刊出版商所有,寻求了解研究成果的研究人员必须订阅该期刊。

sentences.text: A team of researchers working together in the laboratory would submit the results of their research to a journal.
A journal editor would then remove the authors' names and affiliations from the paper and send it to their peers for review.
Depending on the comments received, the editor would accept the paper for publication or decline it.
Copyright rested with the journal publisher, and researchers seeking knowledge of the results would have to subscribe to the journal.
The value of knowledge and the return on the public investment in research depend, in part, upon wide distribution and ready access.
sentences.translation: 知识的价值以及公共研究投资的回报,在一定程度上取决于广泛的传播和便捷的获取。这是一项大生意。在美国,核心科学出版市场的规模估计在70亿至110亿美元之间。国际科学、技术和医学出版商协会表示,全球有2000多家专门从事这些学科的出版商。它们每年在约16000种期刊上发表120多万篇文章。

sentences.text: It is big business.
In America, the core scientific publishing market is estimated at between $7 billion and $11 billion.
The International Association of Scientific, Technical and Medical Publishers says that there are more than 2,000 publishers worldwide specializing in these subjects.
They publish more than 1.2 million articles each year in some 16,000 journals.
The trend in sports, though, may be obscuring an unrecognized reality: Americans have generally stopped growing.
sentences.translation: 然而，体育运动中的这一趋势可能掩盖了一个未被认识到的现实：美国人总体上已经停止长高了。尽管现在通常比140年前高出约两英寸，但今天的人们——尤其是那些出生在已在美国生活了许多代的家庭中的人——显然在20世纪60年代初就达到了他们的极限。而且他们不太可能再长得更高。Wright StateUniversity的人类学家William Cameron Chumlea说："在当今的普通人群中，在这种遗传和环境水平懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2008/section2-part-a-3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好下，我们已经基本达到了我们所能达到的程度。"就NBA球员而言，他们身高的增加似乎源于从世界各地招募球员这一日益普遍的做法。

sentences.text: Though typically about two inches taller now than 140 years ago, today's people – especially those born to families who have lived in the U.S. for many generations – apparently reached their limit in the early 1960s.
And they aren't likely to get any taller.
"In the general population today, at this genetic, environmental level, we've pretty much gone as far as we can go," says anthropologist William Cameron Chumlea of Wright State University.
In the case of NBA players, their increase in height appears to result from the increasingly common practice of recruiting players from all over the world.
Genetically speaking, there are advantages to avoiding substantial height.
sentences.translation: 从遗传学角度来说，避免过高的身高有其优势。在分娩过程中，体型较大的婴儿更难通过产道。此外，尽管人类直立行走已有数百万年，我们的脚和背部仍在与双足姿势作斗争，无法轻易承受超大肢体反复施加的压力。Northwestern University的人类学家William Leonard说："个体有机体的遗传结构设定了一些真正的限制。

sentences.text: During childbirth, larger babies have more difficulty passing through the birth canal.

Moreover, even though humans have been upright for millions of years, our feet and back continue to struggle with bipedal posture and cannot easily withstand repeated strain imposed by oversize limbs.
"There are some real constraints that are set by the genetic architecture of the individual organism," says anthropologist William Leonard of Northwestern University.
Genetic maximums can change, but don't expect this to happen soon.
sentences.translation: 遗传上限可以改变,但不要期望这会很快发生。马萨诸塞州Natick陆军研究中心的高级人类学家Claire C.Gordon确保90%的制服和工作站无需改动即可适合新兵。她说，与篮球制服不同，军装的长度已经有一段时间没有改变了。Gordon说，如果你需要预测不久的将来人类的身高以设计一件设备，总的来说，"你可以使用今天的数据并相当有信心。

sentences.text: Claire C. Gordon, senior anthropologist at the Army Research Center in Natick, Mass., ensures that 90 percent of the uniforms and workstations fit recruits without alteration.
She says that, unlike those for basketball, the length of military uniforms has not changed for some time.
And if you need to predict human height in the near future to design a piece of equipment, Gordon says that by and large, "you could use today's data and feel fairly confident."
That's a far different image from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember from their history books.
sentences.translation: 这与大多数人从历史书中记住的那个砍樱桃树的乔治的形象大不相同。但最近,许多历史学家开始关注奴隶制在开国一代生活中所扮演的角色。他们的研究在一定程度上受到1998年公布的DNA证据的推动,该证据几乎确凿地证明了托马斯·杰斐逊与他的奴隶萨莉·赫明斯至少育有一个孩子。而且仅在过去30年里,学者们才开始自下而上地审视历史。几位历史学家的著作揭示了国家早期领导人所做的道德妥协以及国家初创时期的脆弱本质。更重要的是,他们认为许多开国元勋知道奴隶制是错误的——然而大多数人却几乎没有采取行动反对它。懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2008/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好

sentences.text: But recently, many historians have begun to focus on the role slavery played in the lives of the founding generation.
They have been spurred in part by DNA evidence made available in 1998, which almost certainly proved Thomas Jefferson had fathered at least one child with his slave Sally Hemings.
And only over the past 30 years have scholars examined history from the bottom up.
Works of several historians reveal the moral compromises made by the nation's early leaders and the fragile nature of the country's infancy.
More significantly, they argue that many of the Founding Fathers knew slavery was wrong – and yet most did little to fight it.
More than anything, the historians say, the founders were hampered by the culture of their time.
sentences.translation: 历史学家们说,最重要的是,开国元勋们受到了他们所处时代文化的束缚。虽然华盛顿和杰斐逊私下表达了对奴隶制的反感,但他们也明白奴隶制是他们帮助创建的这个国家的政治和经济基石的一部分。

sentences.text: While Washington and Jefferson privately expressed distaste for slavery, they also understood that it was part of the political and economic bedrock of the country they helped to create.
For one thing, the South could not afford to part with its slaves.
sentences.translation: 首先,南方无法承受失去奴隶的代价。An Imperfect God: George Washington, His Slaves, and theCreation of America一书的作者Wiencek说,拥有奴隶"就像拥有一个巨额银行账户"。如果没有对这种"特殊制度"的保护,南方各州就不会签署宪法,这些保护措施包括一项条款,即为了国会代表权的目的,将一个奴隶算作五分之三个人。

sentences.text: Owning slaves was "like having a large bank account," says Wiencek, author of An Imperfect God: George Washington, His Slaves, and the Creation of America.

The southern states would not have signed the Constitution without protections for the "peculiar institution," including a clause that counted a slave as three fifths of a man for purposes of congressional representation.
And the statesmen's political lives depended on slavery.
sentences.translation: 而且政治家们的政治生涯依赖于奴隶制。五分之三条款通过在选举人团中增加南方各州的票数,使杰斐逊在1800年的总统选举中险胜。上任后,杰斐逊通过1803年的路易斯安那购地案扩大了奴隶制;新的土地被划分为13个州,其中包括三个蓄奴州。

sentences.text: The three-fifths formula handed Jefferson his narrow victory in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College.
Once in office, Jefferson extended slavery with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803; the new land was carved into 13 states, including three slave states.
Still, Jefferson freed Hemings's children – though not Hemings herself or his approximately 150 other slaves.
sentences.translation: 尽管如此,杰斐逊还是释放了赫明斯的孩子们——尽管没有释放赫明斯本人或他大约150名其他奴隶。华盛顿在独立战争期间目睹了黑人士兵的英勇表现后,开始相信人人生而平等,他克服了亲属的强烈反对,在遗嘱中给予他的奴隶们自由。仅仅十年前,这样的行为还需要弗吉尼亚州立法机关的批准。

sentences.text: Washington, who had begun to believe that all men were created equal after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War, overcame the strong opposition of his relatives to grant his slaves their freedom in his will.
Only a decade earlier, such an act would have required legislative approval in Virginia.
